finding.claim: Unauthenticated /preview endpoint fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL server-side and returns status code and first 500 chars of body, with no scheme, host, or IP validation.
finding.source: request.args.get('url') at app.py:15 (GET /preview, no auth guard)

trace.note: requests.get(target) — server-side request to attacker-chosen URL; redirects followed by default
status_code and resp.text[:500] returned to the caller — full-read response channel

finding.guards_checked: None on the path. No auth decorator, no scheme allowlist, no host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP block, no redirect control, no DNS pinning. requests supports only http/https, so file:// is not reachable.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only host check in app.py is the allowlist at app.py:23-25, but it sits in the separate /partner handler (app.py:20-27), not on the /preview path. /preview at app.py:13-17 has no auth decorator, scheme check, host check, or IP block.
verdict.reason: The source `request.args.get("url", "")` at app.py:15 flows unchecked into `requests.get(target, timeout=5)` at app.py:16, and the status code and `resp.text[:500]` are returned to the caller at app.py:17, so an unauthenticated remote attacker can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs and read back the response. The candidate's trace matches the file.

finding.claim: /partner validates the host of the original URL against ALLOWED_HOSTS but fetches with requests, which follows redirects; an allowlisted host that redirects to an internal address causes SSRF. Response exposes only status code (blind).
finding.source: request.args.get('url') at app.py:22 (GET /partner, no auth guard)
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:26 with redirect following enabled

trace.note: host = urlparse(target).hostname — only the initial URL is parsed
requests.get(target) follows redirects by default; redirect hops are not re-validated, so a redirect from an allowlisted host can reach internal/metadata addresses

finding.guards_checked: Hostname allowlist on the initial URL only (app.py:23-25). No scheme check, no re-validation of redirect targets, allow_redirects not disabled, no resolved-IP check. Precondition: attacker controls or can open-redirect an allowlisted partner host. Unverified lead: urlparse and requests/urllib3 may parse edge-case URLs (e.g. backslashes, userinfo) differently, which could bypass the host check; not tested.

verdict.guard_found: app.py:24, `if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS`, exact set membership on urlparse(target).hostname, returning 400 before the sink at app.py:26
verdict.reason: The source at app.py:22 is attacker-controlled and unauthenticated, but app.py:24 is an exact hostname set-membership check on the parsed hostname that runs before the sink, which the rubric counts as a closing guard. Two caveats: the trace is off by one at step 1 (the `@app.route("/partner")` decorator is at app.py:20 and app.py:21 is `def partner():`), and the guard only validates the initial URL, so it does not stop a redirect from an allowlisted host to an internal address at app.py:26 (requests follows redirects by default). If the redirect-to-internal case is what matters, the finding should be re-scoped to that claim rather than closed on the initial-URL check.
